appraisal_events.evidence: elle était apparue à Swann non pas certes sans beauté, mais d'un genre de beauté qui lui était indifférent... lui causait même une sorte de répulsion physique
appraisal_events.explanation: The narration reports Swann's genuine, unflattering aesthetic verdict on Odette's looks, down to specific unappealing features, establishing his initial indifference bordering on distaste.

appraisal_events.evidence: Je comprends que je ne peux rien faire, moi chétive, à côté de grands savants comme vous autres... Je serais comme la grenouille devant l'aréopage... Moi, je n'ai jamais rien à faire ! Je suis toujours libre, je le serai toujours pour vous... je serai trop heureuse d'accourir.
appraisal_events.explanation: Odette flatters Swann's learning and singularity while presenting herself as wholly and permanently available to him; the narrator's aside about the practiced self-satisfaction of her performance lightly ironizes the sincerity of the display.

status_effects.explanation: Swann's private verdict on Odette's beauty is unflattering and even physically repellent to him, locally lowering her in his private estimation.
Odette's flattery and declared total availability place Swann in the position of the courted, admired party who holds the upper hand in the exchange.
Odette casts herself as perpetually free and eager to come whenever summoned, marking her as the emotionally exposed and dependent party in the pursuit.

ambiguities: The narrator's note on Odette's practiced self-satisfaction leaves it unclear how much of her flattery and devotion is genuine versus calculated, affecting whether E2 should be read as sincere admiration or performance.
